Triggers.value: Difficulty breathing or feeling short of breath

Maladaptive Strategies.value: Allowing myself to feel any strong emotion
always sit with back against a wall to see the room
perform mental rituals to prevent bad things from happening again

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are mostly pictures or images.
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to
When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.

Negative Appraisals.value: My life has been destroyed by the trauma
I was betrayed by someone I trusted
I am no longer capable of doing the things that defined me

issues.explanation: The trigger profile implies a vehicle-linked assault context ('Similar cars'), but the rest of the profile does not support a car-related trauma representation. Memory items are generic sensory/intrusive re-experiencing, and the appraisal pattern centers on betrayal by a trusted person, which points more toward an interpersonal assault context than a vehicle-specific cue. This makes the car trigger hard to integrate clinically with the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: 'I was betrayed by someone I trusted' implies the assault involved a trusted perpetrator. That is not impossible, but it sits awkwardly with the selected trigger pattern, especially 'Similar cars' and hypervigilant room-scanning, which suggest threat organized around public/environmental danger rather than betrayal trauma. The profile mixes two fairly different assault formulations without enough overlap to make them cohere.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Sit With Back to Wall: always sit with back against a wall to see the room
issues.explanation: 'Always sit with back against a wall to see the room' reflects ongoing external threat monitoring/hypervigilance. In this formulation, Threat is effectively isolated, with no active links from triggers, memory, or appraisals into Threat. While hypervigilance can occur in PTSD, this particular strategy is not well supported by the rest of the selected items, which are dominated by intrusive memory, betrayal-based appraisals, and emotional avoidance rather than a coherent current-danger theme.

'Similar cars' suggests a vehicle-specific trauma cue (e.g., road traffic incident or assault involving a car), but the rest of the profile centers on betrayal, intrusive sensory memory, and generalized emotional/behavioral responses without any corroborating vehicle-related memory or appraisal content. For an assault profile, this trigger is possible but here it is insufficiently supported and stands out as clinically mismatched.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Sit With Back to Wall: always sit with back against a wall to see the room
issues.explanation: 'Always sit with back against a wall to see the room' reflects persistent external threat monitoring/hypervigilance in current environments. However, the formulation explicitly lacks Threat connections, and the rest of the selected items emphasize intrusive memory, betrayal, and emotion-avoidance rather than ongoing danger monitoring. This strategy therefore fits poorly with the profile structure.

'Similar cars' suggests a vehicle-linked trauma cue, which is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile for an assault trauma: memory and appraisals focus on betrayal and intrusive bodily/image-based recollection rather than a car-centered assault context. This trigger is not impossible, but in this profile it stands out as insufficiently connected to the other selected items.
